sn47.7:1.1: “Bhikkhus, in the Himalayas, the king of mountains, there are rugged and uneven zones where neither monkeys nor human beings can go;
sn47.7:1.2: there are rugged and uneven zones where monkeys can go but not human beings;
sn47.7:1.3: there are even and delightful regions where both monkeys and human beings can go.
sn47.7:1.4: There, along the monkey trails, hunters set out traps of pitch for catching monkeys.
sn47.7:2.1: “Those monkeys who are not foolish and frivolous, when they see the pitch, avoid it from afar.
sn47.7:2.2: But a monkey who is foolish and frivolous approaches the pitch and seizes it with his hand;
sn47.7:2.4: Thinking, ‘I will free my hand,’ he seizes it with his other hand;
sn47.7:2.6: Thinking, ‘I will free both hands,’ he seizes it with his foot;
sn47.7:2.8: Thinking, ‘I will free both hands and my foot,’ he seizes it with his other foot;
sn47.7:2.10: Thinking, ‘I will free both hands and feet,’ he applies his muzzle to it;
sn47.7:2.12: “Thus, bhikkhus, that monkey, trapped at five points, lies there screeching. He has met with calamity and disaster and the hunter can do with him as he wishes.
sn47.7:2.13: The hunter spears him, fastens him to that same block of wood, and goes off where he wants.
sn47.7:2.14: So it is, bhikkhus, when one strays outside one’s own resort into the domain of others.
sn47.7:3.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, do not stray outside your own resort into the domain of others.
sn47.7:3.2: Mara will gain access to those who stray outside their own resort into the domain of others; Mara will get a hold on them.
sn47.7:3.3: “And what is not a bhikkhu’s own resort but the domain of others?
sn47.7:3.5: It is the five cords of sensual pleasure….
sn47.7:3.12: This is what is not a bhikkhu’s own resort but the domain of others.
sn47.7:4.1: “Move in your own resort, bhikkhus, in your own ancestral domain.
sn47.7:4.2: Mara will not gain access to those who move in their own resort, in their own ancestral domain; Mara will not get a hold on them.
sn47.7:4.3: “And what is a bhikkhu’s resort, his own ancestral domain?
sn47.7:4.5: It is the four establishments of mindfulness.
sn47.7:4.7: Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.7:4.8: He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings …
sn47.7:4.10: phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world.
sn47.7:4.11: This is a bhikkhu’s resort, his own ancestral domain.”
